body: The first call to CanActivate return false, The component isn't load the first time. The second time, this is the same route , also the mechanism of instanciation is not fire.

@WilliamKoza You're right. The second time the guard runs, it returns true.

We expect the second check that returns true to result in rendering the component. We see it work if we start at and end up on a non-root path, but not when the redirect ends on root.

For example, try this variation in our Plunker:
1. Click on the "go to something" like to get to `/something`
2. Click the refresh link to reload the app (your URL is still `/something`)
3. Type in `something` so that the guard redirects to `/something` (the same URL you are already at)
4. The component renders this time.

Unfortunately, it's hard to reproduce this issue in Plunker.

The real issue we ran into in our real application is:
1. Navigate to `/search`
2. CanActivate guard redirects using `this.router.navigate([""])` to go to root path
3. Root component has no CanActivate guard
4. Root component does not render
5. The `this.router.navigate` promise is fulfilled as a success, even though the root component did not render.

I am using angular 2.4.0 and angular/router 3.4.1. However the same code works flawlessly with angular/router 3.2.1 and angular 2.4.1

With hash location strategy `RouterModule.forRoot(routes, {useHash: true}),` it works as expected (I believe :))

Adding `{useHash: true}` works, but it inserts a weird `#/` in the URL. This problem doesn't happen on my previous project (A-Cli 1.0.0-beta.20-4 | A 2.2.1), but it happens with latest packages. I thought I was doing something wrong. +1 waiting a correction.
